A cemetery is a place of reverence, reflection, history and continuity. When you create a permanent memorial for a loved one, you’re doing more than laying that person to rest. You’re establishing a legacy that spans the past, present and future.

## Our Cemetery Property

### Custom Estates

A family who wants to stay together may reserve an area of the cemetery exclusively for their loved ones. We design that family’s estate to suit their personal preferences.

PRICING STARTING AT 59,995

### Mausoleum

Some people are more comfortable with the idea of aboveground burial over in-ground burial. Mausoleums, whether private or community, indoors or outdoors, provide that alternative.

PRICING STARTING AT 6,895

- Private
- Community
- Indoor
- Outdoor

Private Mausoleums

#### A legacy that speaks volumes

A very personalized resting place, a private mausoleum conveys a sense of exclusivity and intimacy. It allows a family to have a dedicated burial place that reflects their heritage, values and individuality. It also ensures family members remain together even after death. Customizable in nearly every way, a private mausoleum is a distinguished legacy.

Community Mausoleums

#### A dignified aboveground memorial

Those who wish to create a lasting tribute to their loved ones in a shared space may choose a community mausoleum. An accessible aboveground option, community mausoleums typically house both burial crypts and cremation niches. They often incorporate architectural elements and can foster a sense of connection among families in a community.

Indoor Mausoleums

#### A personalized, protected tribute

Some may value the protection indoor mausoleums provide. They may also appreciate that many indoor mausoleums are climate controlled for year-round comfort. This may be especially important in areas with harsh winters or intense heat. Indoor mausoleum may include spaces for committal services or places for visitors to sit and remember loved ones.

Outdoor Mausoleums

#### A garden setting for memorialization

Open-air mausoleums set among trees and landscaped lawns may appeal to those who find solace in nature. Without a defined walk-in area, garden mausoleums, as outdoor mausoleums are also known, blend in with the environment. Visitors simply walk right up to a loved one’s crypt or niche. Outdoor mausoleum spaces may cost less than those indoors.

### Ground Burial

The time-honored practice of traditional ground burial holds deep cultural and emotional significance for many families. There are ground burial options for both caskets and urns.

PRICING STARTING AT 3,995

#### Casket burial

Casket burial is an enduring tradition with a long history reflecting reverence and the desire for a dignified final resting place for a loved one. Those who choose casket burial for themselves may do so for cultural, religious or personal reasons.

#### Urn burial

More and more people are choosing cremation. Just as a casket can be buried in the ground, so can an urn. Some cemeteries have cremation burial gardens. Some families choose to mix casket burial and urn burial in a single estate.

#### Markers and monuments

When you choose a grave marker, you’re creating a lasting legacy for friends and family to visit for generations to come. Crafted from granite or bronze, monuments and markers can be personalized to tell the stories of unique lives.

### Columbaria

Columbaria house banks of niches for urns. Large or small, private or public, indoors or outdoors, the structures are popular alternatives to cremation burial.

PRICING STARTING AT 3,995

- Indoor
- Outdoor
- Glass-front niches

Indoor

#### A sheltered cremation memorial

Whether standalone building or a room inside another building, an indoor columbarium houses cremation niches. Families may appreciate that many indoor columbaria are climate controlled for comfort, which may be important in areas with harsh weather. Indoor columbaria may include spaces for committal services or places for visitors to sit and reflect.

Outdoor

#### A garden setting for cremation urns

Banks of granite-front or bronze-front cremation niches can be found in community settings or as part of private estates. A columbarium may be part of a cremation garden or simply a standalone structure in another part of a cemetery. These dignified resting places with a connection to nature may hold hundreds of urns or that of a single individual.

Glass-front niche

#### A personalized urn display and more

There are three kinds of cremation niches: bronze front, granite front and glass front. All three can be customized as celebrations of life, but only a glass-front niche allows for the display of personal treasures. Families love glass-front niches because they can see a loved one’s urn as well as a few small reminders of that person whenever they visit.

### Cremation Gardens

Many cemeteries set aside areas for cremation memorials. These cremation gardens may simply be lawn space for burying urns or scattering ashes, or they may be thoughtfully landscaped miniparks.

PRICING STARTING AT 4,995

Cremation Pedestals

#### A monument that sparks memories

Cremation pedestals are small monuments that honor loved ones in personalized ways. Some hold urns; others simply mark burials or scatterings. Common in cremation gardens, slanted niche pedestals appeal to individuals who prefer simpler memorials. Some may choose larger pedestals with custom granite toppers, such as an angel or a guitar.

Cremation Benches

#### An invitation to pause and reflect

Cremation benches memorialize loved ones in much the same way as headstones. Crafted from granite and personalized for those being honored, they may hold as many as four urns or simply mark the places where urns were buried or ashes were scattered. Cremation benches invite cemetery visitors to sit a minute, visit loved ones and reflect.

Photos tell a story but we invite you to see our beautiful cemetery for yourself. You are welcome to visit on your own anytime or let us show you around in person or virtually.

## About

Forest Park East Funeral Home & Cemetery has been a trusted place for families seeking compassion and excellence for generations. The cemetery opened in Webster in 1951, followed by the funeral home in 1989. Together, they provide families from Houston to Galveston with the convenience of planning every detail of a memorial in one serene setting.

Each life deserves to be remembered in a way that feels personal and meaningful. At Forest Park East, celebrations are our specialty. From unicorns and superheroes to motorcycles and more, we’ll help you design a service that reflects the unique passions and personalities of your loved one. With beautifully designed spaces, exclusive services and products, and a concierge style of care, we create gatherings where you can share stories and honor memories with your friends and family.

## A place of compassion for funerals and memorials

Located in the heart of Webster, off Interstate 45, Forest Park East Funeral Home brings you together with the people you love. Our chapel, with its soaring cathedral ceiling and stained-glass accents, is a beautiful place for services. Flexible seating for up to 200 guests makes it feel intimate for smaller gatherings or welcoming for larger celebrations. Closed-circuit television ensures your guests can still see and hear every part of a service, even when the main event space is full.

Beyond the chapel, a spacious reception room provides the perfect backdrop for catered meals or simple gatherings—whether that means coffee and dessert, a sit-down dinner or a breakfast buffet. A coffee bar is also available during visitations and services.

## A peaceful, picturesque memorial park

Spanning more than 143 acres, Forest Park East Cemetery is exceptionally beautiful, with expansive green lawns, tranquil gardens and lakeside spaces designed for quiet reflection. Stately oak and pecan trees shade the meticulously maintained grounds; Clear Creek flows through the cemetery on its way to Clear Lake and the Gulf of Mexico. Here you will find a landscape that inspires peace and remembrance.

You have many beautiful options for creating a lasting place of remembrance. Elegant walled estates are options for companions or families; traditional lawn gardens offer timeless beauty. Indoor and garden mausoleums offer aboveground memorialization. Those choosing cremation may select from columbarium niches or garden burial.

## An inclusive funeral home and cemetery

We welcome families of all faiths, cultures and traditions. Our staff is committed to honoring what matters most to you, working closely to ensure that a service reflects your loved one’s beliefs, values and wishes. No matter your background, we go the extra mile for your family.

This willingness extends across a wide range of meaningful practices. From veterans tributes to a dedicated cemetery section for Jewish families, Forest Park East provides support that honors your family’s heritage with authenticity and care.

### Buddhist traditions

We are among the few funeral homes in the area that permit incense burning. This meaningful accommodation and our knowledgeable staff make us a premier choice for Buddhist services. Our ability to honor these traditions allows Buddhist families to create deeply personal, culturally significant and spiritually comforting ceremonies.

### Veterans tributes

Three cemetery sections are reserved exclusively for veterans. We’re proud to serve veterans and their families with compassion and gratitude, and we arrange military honors with every branch of service. We also participate in the Dignity Memorial® Homeless Veterans Burial Program, ensuring that even those without families receive dignified farewells.

### A sacred space for Jewish families

Though Forest Park East is a nondenominational cemetery, it includes a section for Jewish families affiliated with Congregation Shaar Hashalom. Nonmembers may request permission for a loved one to be buried in this sacred area, giving families a setting reflecting faith and tradition.

## Giving back to our community

Our roots in Webster run deep, and we nurture relationships that last long after a service ends.

Each Mother’s Day, we invite families to gather at the cemetery for a picnic service. It’s a day filled with remembrance and connection, where every mother in attendance receives a flower and more than a thousand blooms are shared with guests to place on the graves of their loved ones. The tradition has become a heartfelt way for families to honor mothers and feel supported during what can be a tender time of year.

In addition, Forest Park East partners with local organizations, such as the Daughters of the American Revolution and area Girl Scouts troops, continuing our commitment to uplift and engage with the community we’re privileged to serve.

## History of Forest Park

The Forest Park brand family began as a single cemetery in 1922. Starting in the 1950s, it was transformed into a full-service funeral and cemetery provider. It later became part of the Dignity Memorial network, while preserving strong local ties and a heritage of excellence.

Whenever you need us, day or night, our compassionate team is here to help. We invite you to visit us and see how we’re different. We’d love to get to know you.
